null_global_scale_is_invariant: by construction: permuting the labels redistributes the same genes, so the total sums and therefore the global fitted scale are the same in every draw

per_chromosome.flag: BELOW MIN_GENES = 100 at 13 genes: reported only, and it enters no statistic, no null and no verdict

reading: NOT CONSISTENT WITH A SINGLE GLOBAL SCALE. The dispersion of the 23 admitted chromosomes' fitted scales about the global scale +0.2150 is Q = 166.048, against a null -- one global scale, the chromosome labels permuted among the same genes with every chromosome's gene count held at its observed value -- whose Q has median 78.9561 and 98.33% range [35.4193, 143.929]: p = 0.003996 against ALPHA 0.05. The secondary range statistic agrees: the observed spread +0.1642 (from +0.1232 on chr13 to +0.2874 on chr14) against a null range of median +0.0950 and 98.33% range [+0.0521, +0.1706], p = 0.013986. SO THE MAGNITUDE THE COMPILED RULES ARE WRONG BY VARIES BETWEEN CHROMOSOMES BY MORE THAN THE SAMPLING NOISE OF THESE GENE COUNTS. THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING AND THIS LANE STOPS HERE: no regional model is proposed, no per-region scale is fitted, no cause is named and no chromosome is read as a verdict about itself. A rejection of gene exchangeability between chromosomes says the fitted scale depends on SOMETHING about the group -- which could be gene density, expression level, rules per gene or gene family as easily as a locus-dependent defect -- and distinguishing those is a separate registration and a separate decision. M2h's one scale +0.2146 and its about 2% of the variance are unaffected as a global average and are not withdrawn by this reading; what is withdrawn is the assumption that one constant is the whole of the correction. The RNA is a measurement already read eight times over and this very spread was already seen post hoc, which makes this a weaker test than one of an unlooked-at pattern. carried with every reading, always: this RNA is not a fresh measurement. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples under the same endpoint was read by items 7, 7d and 7h, by the capped-sum census, by M2h, by M2i, by lane-scalesplit and by lane-recovered, and the P and D grouped here are 7h's committed rows. AND the per-chromosome spread tested here was ALREADY SEEN POST HOC by scalesplit, so this is a test of a pattern that has been looked at, which is weaker than a test of one that has not. A reading here is a statement about THIS measurement's dependence on the chromosome grouping and a hypothesis for a fresh one, not independent confirmation of anything

post_hoc_deciding_nothing.rule: every number in this block decides nothing and can change no verdict; the per-chromosome null bands carry NO correction over the admitted chromosomes and are not a test of any chromosome
post_hoc_deciding_nothing.p_q_against_0_0167: 0.0167 is the 0.05/3 Bonferroni divisor M2h's 98.33% interval came from; the verdict uses 0.05 and only 0.05 (scalehet.ALPHA)

step: 4 of 4: the run, after the registration was committed
question: M2h fitted ONE scale for the whole genome, +0.2146 [98.33% CI +0.2007, +0.2283], and that single number is what makes the compiled rules read better than no rule (held-out Delta MSE +0.04339, about 2% of the variance). lane-scalesplit then reported, POST HOC AND DECIDING NOTHING, within-chromosome scales ranging +0.1232 (chr13) to +0.2874 (chr14), median +0.2176, q1 +0.2041, q3 +0.2376, with no sign change and 10 of 24 inside M2h's interval. THE FALSIFIABLE QUESTION ASKED HERE, AND NO OTHER: IS THAT PER-CHROMOSOME SCALE VARIATION CONSISTENT WITH A SINGLE GLOBAL SCALE? Equivalently: at the gene counts the 24 chromosomes actually carry (chr1 1,700 down to chrY 13), is the observed dispersion of the per-chromosome fitted scales larger than the dispersion a SINGLE global scale would itself produce? The question matters for the MODEL and not for the statistics: one global error is one mis-specified constant in the compiled layer and the repair is one constant; regional variation means the error depends on something about the locus, which is a different defect and a different repair. 'CONSISTENT WITH A SINGLE GLOBAL SCALE' IS A FULL ANSWER AND IS A REACHABLE OUTCOME OF THIS TEST, not a failure to find something
what_is_not_asked: this lane does NOT ask which region has which scale, does NOT fit a per-region scale, does NOT propose a regional model and does NOT read a per-chromosome scale as a verdict about that chromosome. If the test rejects a single global scale, THAT VARIATION EXISTS IS THE FINDING and the lane stops there: fitting per-region scales is a separate registration and a separate decision, which this lane is forbidden to pre-empt. Whatever the outcome, no held-out claim about a new endpoint is made: the chromosome-held-out reading is scalesplit's and is quoted, not re-decided
grouping: BY CHROMOSOME, as 7h's committed table names it, which is a property of the gene's ADDRESS and of no measured value. The chromosome is the region unit for one reason stated in advance: it is the unit scalesplit's post hoc spread was computed on, and this lane's whole purpose is to test that spread rather than a spread of its own choosing. A gene is wholly in one group with all thirteen of its pairs. THE CHROMOSOME IS A COARSE AND ARBITRARY REGION UNIT and that is a LIMITATION, written as one: regional variation at a finer scale -- by compiled element, by locus, by expression level, by rule count -- would not have to show up between chromosomes, so a 'consistent' reading here is consistency BETWEEN CHROMOSOMES and is not a statement about every way the error could vary
no_split: NO TRAINING AND HELD-OUT SPLIT IS USED HERE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE AND IS NOT A WEAKENING. The question is about the DISPERSION OF FITTED SCALES, not about a held-out prediction, so the quantity of interest is in-sample by construction: a per-chromosome scale IS an in-sample fit on that chromosome's genes. A fitted dispersion is biased upward -- 23 scales fitted on 23 groups will differ even when one scale generated them all -- and THE NULL IS WHAT PRICES THAT BIAS EXACTLY, because the null statistic is computed by fitting 23 scales on 23 groups of the same sizes in the same way. Comparing a fitted dispersion to a null of fitted dispersions is the correct comparison; comparing it to zero would not be. The held-out question about whether the calibrated rules beat no rule is M2h's and scalesplit's, is already answered, and is QUOTED here, never re-decided
statistic: PRIMARY, Q: the precision-weighted dispersion of the per-chromosome fitted scales about the global fitted scale. For an admitted chromosome c, let dp_c = sum over that chromosome's pairs of D*P and pp_c = sum over that chromosome's pairs of P^2; its fitted scale is a_c = dp_c / pp_c, which is magcal.FIT applied to that chromosome's rows and nothing else (magcal.fit_scale, imported read-only). Let a_g = (sum over admitted chromosomes of dp_c) / (sum of pp_c), the ONE global scale fitted on the admitted population, which is magcal.fit_scale on exactly those rows. Then Q = sum over admitted chromosomes of pp_c * (a_c - a_g)^2. WHY THAT WEIGHT: under the squared-error fit this calibration minimises, the variance of a_c is proportional to 1 / pp_c, so pp_c is the precision of a_c and pp_c * (a_c - a_g)^2 is each chromosome's squared deviation measured in units of its own noise -- Cochran's homogeneity form. It makes Q large when a PRECISELY fitted chromosome sits far from the global scale and small when a noisily fitted one does, which is the behaviour the question needs. Q IS NOT COMPARED TO A CHI-SQUARED DISTRIBUTION and no asymptotic assumption is made: its null is the permutation null below, so the unknown residual variance cancels and no normality, independence-of-pairs or large-sample claim is required.

SECONDARY, R: the RANGE of the per-chromosome fitted scales, max a_c - min a_c over the admitted chromosomes. This is the statistic the post hoc sentence used ('+0.1232 to +0.2874'), registered here so that the pattern that was looked at is the pattern that is tested. It is REPORTED BESIDE Q AND IS NOT THE VERDICT, for the reason that a range is driven by its two extreme groups and is the less powerful and less stable of the two. Its only registered force is the MIXED outcome below: if Q and R fall on opposite sides of ALPHA the lane says so in the reading and claims neither answer
null_description: THE NULL IS 'ONE GLOBAL SCALE, AND THE PER-CHROMOSOME DEVIATIONS ARE ONLY WHICH GENES HAPPENED TO LAND ON WHICH CHROMOSOME.' It is generated by PERMUTING THE CHROMOSOME LABELS AMONG THE ADMITTED GENES: one permutation draws a uniform random assignment of the admitted genes to the admitted chromosome labels that holds EACH CHROMOSOME'S GENE COUNT EXACTLY AT ITS OBSERVED VALUE (chr1 keeps 1,700 slots, chr13 keeps 280, chr18 keeps 238, and so on), recomputes the 23 per-chromosome scales and the global scale from the permuted grouping by the same formulas, and records Q and R. A GENE IS PERMUTED AS A BLOCK, carrying all thirteen of its pairs, its own P values, its own D values and its own pair sums; no pair is broken apart from its gene and no P is detached from its D. Nothing about any gene's data changes under the null -- only which group it is counted in.

WHY THIS NULL AND NOT ANOTHER, decided now. (1) IT HAS THE SAME PER-CHROMOSOME GENE COUNTS AS THE OBSERVED GROUPING, BY CONSTRUCTION, so it carries the same sampling noise the observed spread was computed at -- which is the precise objection the eye could not answer. (2) IT RESAMPLES WITHIN THE GLOBAL FIT: the whole admitted population, with its one global scale, is the thing being redistributed, so the null is exactly 'these genes, this one scale, a different accident of addresses'. (3) IT IS EXACT UNDER GENE EXCHANGEABILITY and assumes no distribution: it needs no model of the residuals, no variance estimate and no normality, and it prices the upward bias of fitting 23 scales because it fits 23 scales the same way. (4) It uses the REAL genes, so the heavy-tailed, heteroscedastic, decidedly non-normal distribution of real P and D values is present in the null exactly as it is in the observation. WHAT IT ASSUMES, AND THIS IS THE LIMITATION, NOT A CAVEAT: under the null, genes are EXCHANGEABLE between chromosomes. If the genes of one chromosome differ from another's in some way that moves the fitted scale but is not 'the compiled rules are wrong by a different amount there' -- gene density, expression level, rule count per gene, gene family -- then a rejection says the scale depends on SOMETHING ABOUT THE GROUP and does not say what. A rejection is therefore a finding of heterogeneity between chromosomes and NOT an identification of its cause, and this lane will not name one.

PERMUTATION COUNT AND SEED, FIXED NOW: PERMUTATIONS['count'] = 1000 draws at PERMUTATIONS['seed'] = 20261012, one numpy default_rng seeded once. 1000 is magcal's own permutation count, taken unchanged. The smallest attainable p is 1/(1+1000) = 0.000999, which is far below ALPHA, so the test CAN reject; and 1000 draws resolve a p near ALPHA = 0.05 to about +-0.007 (one standard error), which is stated as the resolution of the p and is not refined after the fact
alpha: ALPHA = 0.05, one-sided, magcal.CONTROL_ALPHA taken UNCHANGED, AND THE CHOICE IS DELIBERATELY THE ONE THAT MAKES THIS LANE'S EXPECTED ANSWER THE HARDER TO OBTAIN. The expected answer is 'consistent with a single global scale', which is a FAILURE TO REJECT; a strict threshold would make failing to reject easy and the reading cheap. 0.05 is the LAXER of the two defensible thresholds available -- the other being 0.0167, the 0.05/3 Bonferroni divisor M2h's 98.33% interval came from -- so adopting 0.05 gives heterogeneity the EASIER passage and makes a 'consistent' reading the harder result to reach. The p against 0.0167 is reported beside it as a descriptive so a reader can see both, but THE VERDICT USES 0.05 AND ONLY 0.05. CORRECTION, DECIDED NOW: there are TWO registered readings in this lane, Q (primary) and R (secondary), and NO Bonferroni correction is applied to ALPHA over them -- for the same reason: splitting 0.05 between them would halve the chance of detecting heterogeneity and so inflate the chance of the expected 'consistent' answer. Instead the multiplicity is handled by the MIXED outcome, which refuses to pick a side when the two statistics disagree, so an uncorrected pair of tests cannot buy a cleaner verdict than the evidence supports. This lane registers NO interval that excludes 0 and makes NO claim of an effect's sign, so the 98.33% width is used only to DESCRIBE the null's spread (see INTERVAL) and never to decide
interval: 98.33% percentile interval, magcal.FORM_INTERVAL taken UNCHANGED, DECIDED NOW AND NOT AFTER, and used for DESCRIPTION, with the verdict resting on the permutation p alone. What it is placed on, fixed here: (1) the NULL DISTRIBUTION OF Q -- its 98.33% percentile range and its median -- so a reader can see the observed Q against the range a single global scale itself produces; (2) the NULL DISTRIBUTION OF R, the same way, which is the direct answer in the units of the sentence that prompted this lane: how wide a min-to-max spread of per-chromosome scales does ONE global scale generate at these gene counts? (3) per admitted chromosome, the null's 98.33% range of THAT CHROMOSOME'S OWN fitted scale at its own gene count, beside its observed scale -- 23 bands, each deciding nothing, carrying NO correction over 23 and therefore NOT A TEST of any chromosome, named a descriptive here so it cannot later be read as 23 verdicts. WHY 98.33%: it is the width M2h and scalesplit's committed readings are stated at, so every number this lane prints beside theirs is at the same width and a comparison is not also a comparison of widths; and it is what magcal's own functions compute, which this lane calls read-only rather than editing magcal's file
which_governs: THE PERMUTATION p OF Q DECIDES, at ALPHA = 0.05, one-sided. R's p can only turn a verdict into MIXED; it can never, by itself, declare either answer. No interval, no descriptive, no per-chromosome band and no context number from M2h, 7h or scalesplit may change the verdict. The outcome is the registered function of (p_Q, p_R, the admitted chromosome count, the null's degeneracy) and of nothing else, and it is computed by `decide_heterogeneity` below, which is planted in all of its directions by tests/test_scalehet.py
not_vacuous: the test can come out either way and both outcomes are statements. If the per-chromosome scales were driven by real regional variation, Q would exceed the dispersion that label permutation produces and p_Q would be small -- the floor 0.000999 is attainable at 1000 draws. If one global scale generated them, Q would sit inside the null's bulk and p_Q would be large. A planted test holds each direction: genes on one chromosome given a different slope must read HETEROGENEOUS, and genes whose slope is identical everywhere must read CONSISTENT_WITH_ONE_SCALE. THE OUTCOME IS NOT PREDETERMINED BY THE DESIGN, and 'consistent' is reported as a FULL ANSWER and not as an absence
falsifier: THE CLAIM UNDER TEST IS 'ONE GLOBAL SCALE': that the per-chromosome scales differ only by which genes landed on which chromosome. IT IS FALSIFIED by p_Q <= 0.05 -- an observed precision-weighted dispersion larger than 95% of the dispersions a single global scale produces at these very gene counts -- in which case this lane reports HETEROGENEOUS and 'the magnitude is one constant' may not be said. IT IS NOT FALSIFIED by p_Q > 0.05, in which case the lane reports CONSISTENT_WITH_ONE_SCALE, which is a FULL ANSWER to the question asked and not an absence of one. WHAT WOULD HAVE FALSIFIED THE OPPOSITE CLAIM: 'the magnitude varies by region' predicts a Q above the null's 98.33% range and an observed spread wider than the null's; a Q sitting at the null's median is that prediction failing. WHAT 'INCONCLUSIVE' IS, exactly and in advance: fewer than MIN_CHROMOSOMES = 10 chromosomes admitted; an undefined global or per-chromosome fit; a degenerate null Q distribution; or the harness missing, which is reported as HARNESS_DEFECT. INCONCLUSIVE IS NOT a p near the threshold, which is reported with its value and decided by the table, and it is NOT the MIXED case, which is its own named outcome. WHAT NEITHER OUTCOME CAN SAY: neither can identify what makes a scale differ, neither can speak about regions finer than a chromosome, neither revises M2h's about 2% of the variance, and neither makes a scale an explanation of expression rather than a magnitude correction
prior_exposure: STATED PLAINLY, AND NOT A CAVEAT ADDED AFTERWARDS. THIS IS A RE-ANALYSIS OF A MEASUREMENT ALREADY READ, NOT A FRESH TEST. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples, under the same log2(TPM+1) endpoint and the same no-rule baseline, has already been read by: item 7 (M2b, lane-readercompile) including its post-hoc information term; item 7d (M2c, lane-combine2) for the runtime's mean and promoter competition; item 7h (M2f, lane-multrna) for the multiplicative composition; the capped-sum census (lane-capsumrna), which reached NOT_TESTABLE; M2h (lane-magcal), which fitted the one scale and read 'better' on a random split; M2i (lane-freshrna), which replicated it with nothing fitted on RNA fresh to this project; lane-scalesplit, which re-split the same rows by chromosome; and lane-recovered. The P and D this lane groups by chromosome ARE 7h's committed rows, which are the rows M2h calibrated and scalesplit re-split, SO EVERY VALUE THIS LANE READS HAS BEEN READ BEFORE.

AND, SEPARATELY AND MORE SHARPLY: THE PER-CHROMOSOME SPREAD ITSELF WAS ALREADY SEEN. scalesplit computed and committed all 24 per-chromosome scales as post hoc descriptives, and the range (+0.1232 chr13 to +0.2874 chr14), the median (+0.2176), the quartiles (+0.2041, +0.2376), the absence of a sign change and the count inside M2h's interval (10 of 24) are in data/results/scalesplit_result.json and in this lane's brief. THIS LANE IS THEREFORE TESTING A PATTERN THAT HAS BEEN LOOKED AT, WHICH IS WEAKER THAN TESTING ONE THAT HAS NOT. Specifically: the statistic is registered before it is computed, but it is registered by someone who already knows roughly how wide the observed spread is and which two chromosomes sit at its ends; a statistic chosen after seeing a pattern can be chosen to flatter it, in either direction. Two things are done about that and neither removes it. (1) The PRIMARY statistic is a weighted dispersion over ALL admitted chromosomes, not a statistic about chr13 or chr14, and no chromosome is named in it. (2) The statistic the eye actually used -- the RANGE, max minus min, which is the +0.1232-to-+0.2874 sentence -- is registered too, as a SECONDARY reading, precisely so that the pattern that was looked at is the pattern that is tested, and so that a disagreement between the two cannot be quietly dropped. Any reading from this lane holds as a statement about THIS measurement's dependence on the chromosome grouping. It is not independent confirmation of M2h, it is not a blind prediction of an unseen measurement, and a 'consistent' reading is consistency at these gene counts and this grouping, not a proof that one constant is exactly right
prior_exposure_clause: carried with every reading, always: this RNA is not a fresh measurement. The same ENCODE polyA plus RNA-seq of the same thirteen reader biosamples under the same endpoint was read by items 7, 7d and 7h, by the capped-sum census, by M2h, by M2i, by lane-scalesplit and by lane-recovered, and the P and D grouped here are 7h's committed rows. AND the per-chromosome spread tested here was ALREADY SEEN POST HOC by scalesplit, so this is a test of a pattern that has been looked at, which is weaker than a test of one that has not. A reading here is a statement about THIS measurement's dependence on the chromosome grouping and a hypothesis for a fresh one, not independent confirmation of anything
stop_rule: one run of scripts/scalehet_run.py, after this registration is committed. The statistic, the null, the permutation count, the seed, the gene floor, the admitted-chromosome minimum, the threshold and the decision table are fixed here and are not revisited after a number is seen. NOTHING IS RE-RUN AT ANOTHER SEED, another permutation count, another gene floor or another region unit, and the run refuses to overwrite its own result file. If the outcome is HETEROGENEOUS, no per-region scale is fitted by this lane under any circumstances
limitations: THE REGION UNIT IS THE CHROMOSOME, which is coarse and biologically arbitrary. It was chosen because it is the unit the post hoc spread was computed on, so that this lane tests that spread rather than one of its own choosing. Regional variation by compiled element, by locus, by expression level or by rules per gene need not show between chromosomes, so a 'consistent' reading is consistency BETWEEN CHROMOSOMES and nothing wider

THE NULL ASSUMES GENES ARE EXCHANGEABLE BETWEEN CHROMOSOMES. A rejection therefore says the fitted scale depends on something about the group, not that the compiled rules' error is locus-dependent; gene density, expression level, rules per gene and gene family would all produce it. This lane names no cause

GENES THAT SHARE A COMPILED ELEMENT ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. The permutation unit is the GENE, so correlation between genes within a chromosome is NOT priced into the null, and if it is substantial the null's Q is too narrow and p_Q is anti-conservative -- the error runs toward DETECTING heterogeneity, which is against this lane's expected answer and so does not flatter it. An element-level or locus-block permutation is not registered and is not computed: it would need a gene-to-element map this lane does not build, and naming it as the fix is a separate registration

A FAILURE TO REJECT IS NOT A PROOF OF IDENTITY. The null's own 98.33% Q range and the null's range of per-chromosome spreads are reported as the honest measure of what this test could have detected: a regional variation smaller than that spread would not be seen here

NO HELD-OUT PREDICTION IS MADE BY THIS LANE. The statistic is in-sample by construction and the null prices that exactly; the held-out reading that the calibrated rules beat no rule is M2h's and scalesplit's, is quoted verbatim, and is not re-decided here

THE RNA IS A MEASUREMENT ALREADY READ, by items 7, 7d, 7h, the capped-sum census, M2h, M2i, scalesplit and lane-recovered, AND THE SPREAD TESTED HERE WAS ALREADY SEEN POST HOC. Both are stated in PRIOR_EXPOSURE and both weaken every reading below what the same test on an unlooked-at pattern in a fresh measurement would carry

A SCALE IS A MAGNITUDE CORRECTION AND NEVER AN EXPLANATION OF EXPRESSION. Whatever this lane reads, the calibrated compiled rules buy about 2% of the variance on M2h's held-out side, and that number is not improved, revised or reinterpreted by anything here
descriptives: deciding nothing, reported beside the registered reading: every admitted chromosome's fitted scale with its gene count, pair count, dp_c, pp_c and weighted squared deviation, in the order the deviation ranks; the excluded chromosomes' scales and counts, FLAGGED as below MIN_GENES and entering no statistic; the global fitted scale on the admitted population and on all 24 chromosomes, beside M2h's committed +0.2146; the null distributions of Q and R, each with its median, its 98.33% percentile range and its minimum and maximum over the 1000 draws; per admitted chromosome, the null's 98.33% range of that chromosome's own scale at its own gene count beside its observed scale, with NO correction over 23 and therefore NOT a test of any chromosome; the descriptive p of Q against 0.0167 as well as against 0.05; how many admitted chromosomes lie inside M2h's committed scale interval and how many have a negative scale; and the median, quartiles, minimum and maximum of the admitted per-chromosome scales, recomputed here so that scalesplit's post hoc sentence is reproduced rather than quoted from memory

parameters.grouping: by chromosome, as 7h's committed table names it
parameters.statistic: Q = sum over admitted chromosomes of pp_c * (a_c - a_g)^2; R = max a_c - min a_c
parameters.null: the chromosome labels permuted among the genes, each group's gene count held exactly
parameters.free_parameters: one closed-form scale per admitted chromosome and one global scale; the null refits every one of them on each draw, so nothing fitted here is unpriced

exclusions: chrY: fewer than MIN_GENES = 100 genes in 7h's committed table, by the floor fixed in the registration before any value of this lane was read

partitions.grouping: by chromosome; a gene is wholly in one group with all thirteen of its pairs
partitions.held_out: none, by registration (scalehet.NO_SPLIT): the statistic is a dispersion of FITTED scales and the permutation null prices the in-sample fitting exactly

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 036eec6

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
